title: Edmund and the Harbor
premise: In the winter of the great storms, Sable Underhill keeps the harbor light and tells himself that history belongs to cities, not to a widower with an empty workshop. When a frightened child is left at his door with a note reading 'forget the face,' Sable recognizes the boy as the son of a smuggler he once loved, and hiding him means finishing the boat hidden in the workshop before the river ice breaks. As soldiers comb the coast, Sable must choose between the safety of invisibility and the dangerous work of remembering. He launches the boat in a storm, loses the lighthouse to fire, and sends the boy upriver to freedom—surviving, but no longer able to pretend he was never part of anything.
about_author: Lior Underhill is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the northern coast. This is their second novel, written in a coastal town where the fog still arrives on schedule.

chapters.title: The Light That Keeps Nothing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine winter night at the light establishes his grief, his half-finished boat, and his creed of invisibility—until a knock reveals a child frozen at the door, clutching a note in handwriting Sable knows too well. Emotional beat: the crack in a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Instructions for Forgetting
chapters.summary: Alternating between Sable's present care for the boy, Tomas, and memories of Ilse, the smuggler he loved and lost to duty's demands. Soldiers begin asking questions at the harbor; Sable burns one letter and cannot burn another. Emotional beat: memory as both wound and compass.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, rising tension. The river ice groans toward breaking; the search tightens; a neighbor betrays suspicion. Racing to finish the boat by lamplight, Sable teaches Tomas the river's secrets, and the boy's trust forces him to admit what survival has cost him. Emotional beat: love reassembling itself against duty.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Harbor
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution. On the night the ice breaks, soldiers reach the lighthouse; Sable fires the lamp one last time as a decoy while Tomas slips downriver in the finished boat. The light tower burns; Sable watches from the water's edge, finally visible, finally part of history. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into witness.
